tools.name: schedule_get_request
tools.description: Create one schedule that sends a GET to a public URL later: once at an exact time (run_at) or repeatedly (cron). Pass exactly one of run_at or cron. The URL is one the person supplies; RunLater does not limit it to a particular API. Nothing is sent now. RunLater sends it at the scheduled time, retri

tools.name: schedule_send_request
tools.description: Create one schedule that sends a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE to a public URL later, with an optional body: once at an exact time (run_at) or repeatedly (cron). Pass exactly one of run_at or cron. Nothing is sent now. The URL is one the person supplies; RunLater does not limit it to a particular API.

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description: List scheduled requests in this workspace, newest first, with status (scheduled, paused or finished) and next run time.

tools.name: get_schedule
tools.description: Get one scheduled request with its recent runs: status code, duration, error and a preview of each response. Use this to check whether a request worked.

tools.name: pause_schedule
tools.description: Pause a scheduled request so it stops running until resumed.

tools.name: resume_schedule
tools.description: Resume a paused request. A recurring one continues at its next cron time. A one-time one needs its run time to still be in the future.

tools.name: run_now
tools.description: Send a scheduled request once, right now, without retries, and return the status code and response. A successful run counts toward the monthly limit. A one-time request is finished after this.

tools.name: delete_schedule
tools.description: Delete a scheduled request for good. It stops running and cannot be restored.

tools.name: account_status
tools.description: Show this workspace's limits and usage this month. If it doesn't have access yet, the result says where to go next.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: schedule_get_request · Public sink: schedule_send_request, run_now · Destructive: schedule_get_request, schedule_send_request, list_schedules, resume_schedule, run_now, delete_schedule.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: schedule_get_request · Public sink: schedule_send_request, run_now · Destructive: schedule_get_request, schedule_send_request, list_schedules, resume_schedule, run_now, delete_schedule

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "account_status" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Show this workspace's plan, trial end date, limits and usage this month. With no plan yet, it includes the link where the 14-day trial starts." → after: "Show this workspace's limits and usage this month. If it doesn't have access yet, the result says where to go next."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
